issues.description: ValueError for unsupported delimiter is the wrong exception class and fires inconsistently.
issues.detail: Bad-delimiter validation only runs when the param is present and the value is a single string; if the param is absent or already a list, an invalid delimiter is silently accepted. Also, ValueError flows through the same channel docstring says becomes HTTPBadRequest, conflating programmer error with client error. Validate up front and use TypeError or a dedicated exception.

issues.description: delimiter is silently a no-op when the value is already a list (auto_parse_qs_csv or multi-instance).
issues.detail: When items arrived pre-split, delimiter is ignored without warning, making behavior depend on request shape and parser config. The asymmetry is only half-documented. Either document loudly as the explicit contract or raise so callers learn their assumption is wrong.

issues.description: delimiter argument complects a literal character with an OpenAPI style name in one string slot.
issues.detail: _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS routes both ',' and 'spaceDelimited' through one parameter and one lookup. These are different kinds of values sharing a string-typed slot, which surprises callers and complects the splitting story already shared by multi-instance values and auto_parse_qs_csv. Consider exposing style constants as named module attributes the caller resolves explicitly.

issues.description: _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS dict has redundant identity entries that obscure the contract.
issues.detail: Three of five entries map a character to itself; the dict is doing membership-validation and alias-resolution at once. A frozenset of accepted characters plus a small alias dict for the two style names would state intent more clearly and make error messages honest about which set was violated.

issues.description: No test covers delimiter combined with the transform callback.
issues.detail: Tests cover comma, space, pipe, unsupported delimiter, csv interaction, and multi-value, but not the natural split-then-cast pattern (e.g. delimiter+int). The split-vs-transform ordering invariant is also undocumented. Add one test and state the invariant in the docstring so a future refactor cannot silently flip semantics.

issues.description: delimiter default in @overload signatures uses `= None` instead of `= ...`.
issues.detail: The surrounding six overloads on the same function use `= ...` per typing convention; the new delimiter keyword breaks that voice with `= None`. Functionally identical, but inconsistent with the file's existing style. Match the surrounding overloads.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK for a small, well-scoped patch adding a delimiter kwarg to get_param_as_list. Two P1s must land before merge: ValueError on bad delimiter fires inconsistently (only when the param is present and a single string) and uses the wrong exception class given the HTTPBadRequest contract; and delimiter silently no-ops when the value is already a list, making behavior depend on request shape and parser config. A third P1 from Hickey flags that the delimiter argument complects a literal character with an OpenAPI style name through one string-typed slot. Remaining P2s are housekeeping: the identity-laden _PARAM_VALUE_DELIMITERS dict, missing delimiter+transform test coverage with an undocumented ordering invariant, and an overload-signature style inconsistency.
